chunks: That is a day in which Allah will gather the first and the last for the reckoning of accounts and the recompense of deeds, in humility, standing, with sweat reaching their mouths, and the earth trembling beneath them; the best of them in condition is he who finds a place for his two feet and an open space for his breath.

key_terms.الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ: The first and the last (all of humanity)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition of people on the Day of Judgment according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali describes the Day of Judgment as a universal gathering for reckoning, emphasizing the profound physical distress where the earth trembles and sweat overwhelms humanity. Scholarly tradition interprets the 'ease' for the fortunate not merely as physical comfort, but as the spiritual relief of those whose deeds have secured their standing before God, contrasting with the general anxiety of the masses. This imagery underscores the Shia emphasis on the tangible reality of the afterlife and the ultimate justice of divine recompense.

en.sayed-ali-raza: That day would be such that Allāh would collect on it the anteriors and the posteriors, to stand in obedience for exaction of accounts and for award of recompense for deeds. Sweat would flow upto their mouths like reins while earth would be trembling under them.
In the best condition among them would be he who has found a resting place for both his feet and an open place for his breath.
